label: L009UiGS-2HaxD-IN
description: MikroTik L009UiGS-2HaxD-IN (L009UiGS-2HaxD-IN) - 8x 1G RJ45, 1x SFP, Wi-Fi 2.4 GHz. Powered by the DC jack or by 802.3af/at PoE-in on eth1 only (24-56 V); passive PoE-out on eth8. ARM 32bit 2-core IPQ-5018.
notes: Vendor rows read 2026-11-28 from https://mikrotik.com/product/l009uigs_2haxd_in: **PoE in 802.3af/at**, **PoE in input Voltage 24-56 V**, **Max power consumption without attachments 14 W**, **PoE-out ports Ether8**, **PoE out Passive PoE**, and the marketing copy names both ends: "There's PoE-in on the first port. You can use it instead of the DC jack to power the unit. And there's PoE-Out* on the last port - for powering other devices." So `eth1` is the inlet and draws the 14 W board ceiling (the direct replacement for the earlier `poeIn: true`, which stated no wattage at all); `eth2`-`eth7` declare poeIn: false; `eth8` sources passive PoE and is not a PD. The six sockets beside the inlet had been inheriting the 12.95 W 802.3af guess from `category: wireless`, 77.7 W from a 14 W router.
